To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the adaptation to cold in combination with high-mountain hypobaric hypoxia leads to the development of more pronounced changes in the structure of the diaphragmatic muscular fibers and hepatocytes than in adaptation to the cold in normobarometric conditions.

the peculiarities of quantitative parameters of hepatocytes and diaphragm muscle fibres revealed in conditions of long-term effect of cold in normobar and hypobar conditions indicate different efficiency of adaptation in organs depending on the character and organ specificity of the effect.

the peculiarities of hepatocytes and muscle fiber changes in diaphragm of albino rats under the effect of cold and combined effect of cold with hypoxia indicate the organ-specificity of adaptation and the different efficiency of adaptive reactions depending on the character and intensity of the effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the fact that in the conditions of the long-lasting effect of low temperatures and its combination with high-altitudinal hypoxia the adaptive changes in the hepatocytes and diaphragm muscle fibers are characterized by a different direction and degree of manifestation.

the study of the morphometric characteristics of the diaphragmatic muscle and liver cells of albino rats under the influence of cold and high mountain hypoxiosis, and also the combined effects of these factors.

the fact that in conditions of the combined effect of cold with high-mountain hypobaric hypoxia the processes of adaptation of the body to the stress are realized in more intensive way in comparison with adaptation to cold in the normobaric conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adaptation of the body to cold is a complicated and multi-factorial process, which involves a variety of mechanisms of regulation and adaptation at the cellular, organ, and organism levels.
in the adaptation to the cold, in normobaric and hypobaric conditions, the dynamics of quantitative characteristics of diaphragm muscle fibres and hepatocyte are different.

in conditions of the combined effect of cold with high mountain hypoxic conditions the adaptation process of hepatocytes and diaphragm muscular fibre are similar to the adaptation to cold in normal conditions, but their intensity is increased.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adaptation of rats to cold and high-moutain hypoxia in combination with cold is a complicated process, which is accompanied by changes of the quantitative indexes of the hepatocytes and the diaphragm muscle fibers.
the cold is a factor that is more efficient for adaptation of the diaphragmatic muscles than the hypobaric hypoxia.

in conditions of the combined effect of the long-term exposure of cold and high mountain hypoxias the adaptive mechanisms in the organism are realized in the different directions and the efficiency of the adaptive processes depends on the character of exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

adaptation of the organism to the combined effect of cold exposure and high-mountainous hypoxia leads to more significant morphological changes of diaphragm muscles and liver than adaptation to cold alone.

the combined effect of cold (2-5 C for 40 days) and high-mountain (4000 m height) hypoxia on the diaphragm muscle fibers and liver cells of rats is accompanied by the increase of the relative volume of mitochondria in both organs, while the volumetric index of rough endoplamic reticulum and the glycogen content in the cells of liver are decreased.
the combination of the cold and high-altitude hypobaric hypoxia leads to more pronounced changes in the hepatocytes and muscular fibers of the diaphram than in the cold alone.
